criteria.no: The item text is silent about the directive: it neither includes the directive's specific content nor references it.
criteria.unclear: The item text alludes to the directive's topic but it is not possible to tell whether the directive itself is included.
criteria.yes: The item text contains the directive's specific content, in its own words or the user's, as a step, constraint, or stated starting point.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` explicitly carry out, preserve, or plan for the directive given in `anchor.statement`? Look for the directive's specific content being present in the item: the same starting point, the same method, the same constraint, or an explicit step that does what the statement asks. A generic mention of the topic without the directive's specific content does not count. Judge presence of the directive only, not whether the item conflicts with it.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item text conflicts with the directive, whether or not the directive is mentioned.
criteria.unclear: The item text is ambiguous enough that it might or might not conflict with the directive.
criteria.yes: The item text states a plan, approach, or decision that cannot be reconciled with the directive in the anchor statement.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` propose doing something that `anchor.statement` rules out, or propose a different approach than the one `anchor.statement` requires? Examples of contradiction: the anchor says to start from an existing implementation and the item plans a fresh implementation; the anchor forbids a dependency and the item adds it; the anchor fixes an order of work and the item reverses it. Silence about the directive is not a contradiction. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item is about a different part of the system or a different activity, and completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell what part of the system it touches.
criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about, directly or as a clear prerequisite.

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.

criteria.no: The item lacks that requirement: no manifest, no per-file hashes, an archive-level hash only, or hashes for only part of the shipped files.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions hashes or a manifest but does not settle whether every shipped file has one.
criteria.yes: The item requires a published manifest containing a hash for each shipped skill file, including agents, skills and Python files.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` require the published skill to carry a manifest with the hash of every shipped file, so each installed file can be checked against it? The required content is per-file hashes covering all shipped files, recorded in a published manifest. Judge presence only.

criteria.no: The item states no such decision; silence, a compliant plan, or omitting non-shipped repository files is no conflict.
criteria.unclear: The item may ship some files without hashes, but it cannot be told.
criteria.yes: The item decides to ship some files unhashed, to publish only an archive-level hash, or to publish no manifest.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` state a decision under which the published manifest would not hold a hash of every shipped file? Silence about the manifest is not conflict.

criteria.no: The item concerns a different activity than publishing the atm-bd skill, such as LLM call retries.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions packaging or hashing but not clearly for the atm-bd skill.
criteria.yes: The item concerns publishing or packaging the atm-bd skill, or the manifest or file hashes published with it.

relevant.instructions: The anchor is about what the atm-bd skill ships when it is published so an installer can verify files. Does `item.text` touch publishing the atm-bd skill or the file hashes and manifest that ship with it? Judge subject overlap only.

criteria.no: The item does not require a hash of every shipped file: it is silent, mentions integrity or verification only in general, hashes only the archive as a whole, or hashes only some shipped files.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions a manifest or file hashes but it cannot be told whether every shipped file gets a hash.
criteria.yes: The item states that the published skill ships a manifest or hash list containing a hash for each shipped file, in wording such as every file, each file, or all agent, skill and Python files.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` require the published skill to include a manifest that records a hash (for example a SHA-256) of every shipped file, as `anchor.statement` requires? Shipped files include the skill's agent, skill and Python files. Judge presence only, not conflict.

criteria.no: No explicit incompatible decision exists: the item is silent about hashes or manifests, or leaves out only files that are not shipped in the skill.
criteria.unclear: The item may leave some shipped files unhashed, but which files are shipped or hashed is unresolved.
criteria.yes: The item states that a shipped file is left unhashed or out of the manifest, that only a whole-archive hash is published instead of per-file hashes, or that no manifest is published.

contradicted.instructions: Does an explicit decision in `item.text` prevent the published skill's manifest from holding a hash of every shipped file? Silence is not conflict.

criteria.no: The item concerns a different activity, such as runtime retry behavior or task assignment, and does not touch skill publishing.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions a release or package but it cannot be told whether it concerns publishing the atm-bd skill.
criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on publishing or releasing the atm-bd skill, its package contents, or a release manifest or hash list.

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` touch how the atm-bd skill is published or released, including what the published package contains, a release manifest, or file hashes shipped with it? Judge subject overlap only; the item need not mention hashes to be relevant.

criteria.no: No when the item has no such manifest: silence, general integrity or tamper detection, one hash of the whole archive, or hashes of only some shipped files.
criteria.unclear: Unclear when the item mentions a manifest of hashes but its coverage of the shipped files cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: Yes when the item has the published skill carry a manifest with a hash for each shipped file (every file, each file, the entire skill, all agents/skills/python files).

addressed.instructions: Is a per-file hash manifest for the published skill present in `item.text`: one manifest, shipped with the skill, with a hash entry for every shipped file? Judge presence only.

criteria.no: The item commits to nothing that leaves a shipped file unhashed; it may be silent, compliant, or exclude files that are not part of the shipped skill.
criteria.unclear: The item's approach might leave some shipped files unhashed, but it is ambiguous.
criteria.yes: The item commits to an approach that leaves shipped files unhashed: only some file kinds hashed, only one whole-archive hash, or no manifest at all.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` commit to a publication approach under which some shipped file of the skill has no hash in the published manifest? Silence is not a contradiction.

criteria.no: Completing the item would neither publish the atm-bd skill nor change its release package or manifest.
criteria.unclear: It cannot be told from the item whether it touches the atm-bd skill release.
criteria.yes: The item plans, changes or depends on the published atm-bd skill package, its release process, or its integrity manifest.

relevant.instructions: Does the work in `item.text` touch the atm-bd skill release: what is published, how the published package is built or verified, or a manifest of file hashes? Judge overlap of subject only.

criteria.no: The item is silent about per-file hashes, describes integrity checks without a per-file manifest, hashes only the release archive, or hashes only a subset of shipped files.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions per-file hashes but does not say which files they cover.
criteria.yes: The item says a manifest published with the skill records a hash for each file the skill ships, or for every agent, skill and Python file, which together cover all shipped files.

addressed.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires a manifest in the published skill holding a hash for every shipped file. Does `item.text` state that obligation for the complete set of shipped files, not just some of them? Judge presence only.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item rules out a per-file hash manifest; it is silent, compliant, or omits only files that are not shipped.
criteria.unclear: The item may exclude some shipped files from hashing but it is ambiguous whether those files are shipped.
criteria.yes: The item explicitly leaves some shipped files without a hash, replaces per-file hashes with one archive hash, or publishes no manifest.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` decide something that rules out a published manifest holding a hash of every shipped file? Examples: a shipped file kind is left without a hash, a single archive hash replaces per-file hashes, or no manifest is published. Silence and leaving out files that are not shipped are not conflict.

criteria.no: The item is about another part of the system, for example slot retries, task closing or the console, and not about publishing the skill.
criteria.unclear: The item is too vague to tell whether it concerns publishing the atm-bd skill.
criteria.yes: The item is about publishing, releasing or packaging the atm-bd skill, or about its release manifest or file hashes.

relevant.instructions: The anchor governs atm-bd skill publishing. Does `item.text` plan or change the publication of the atm-bd skill: building, releasing or packaging it, or the manifest and hashes that accompany a release? Judge subject overlap only.
